slot.brief: Compare cloudiness appearance time for a primary, secondary and tertiary alcohol with Lucas reagent; ask which reacts immediately and why.

stem: On adding Lucas reagent to primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols, which one gives immediate cloudiness, and why?
options: Primary alcohol; it forms the most stable carbocation
Secondary alcohol; it forms the most stable carbocation
Tertiary alcohol; it reacts by an $S_{N2}$ mechanism
Tertiary alcohol; it forms the most stable carbocation

verdicts.working: Tertiary alcohols form the most stable carbocations, so they react fastest by the SN1 pathway and give immediate cloudiness.

working:
Lucas reaction proceeds mainly by $\text{S}_\text{N}1$.\
Carbocation stability: tertiary $>$ secondary $>$ primary.\
Thus a tertiary alcohol gives immediate cloudiness.

Independent check: Tertiary alcohols form the most stable carbocations, so they react fastest by the SN1 pathway and give immediate cloudiness.
solution:
Lucas reaction proceeds mainly by the $S_N1$ mechanism, whose rate depends on carbocation stability:
$$3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$$
Tertiary alcohol forms the most stable carbocation and reacts fastest, giving immediate cloudiness.
